title: cost-optimization-autotune-defaults-batching-caching-quant-uecon-tooling
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: Reduce per-token unit cost for common Redwood workloads by automating sensible defaults and providing deterministic tooling for unit-econ evaluation. This PR introduces: 1) an autotune service that recommends batching and KV caching defaults per model/class of workload, 2) a quantization profile registry and picker integrated with the serving runtime, and 3) a unit-economics CLI and dashboard plumbing to evaluate cost/latency tradeoffs for candidate configs. The goal is not to force a single configuration but to: provide safe defaults for new customers, enable operators to opt into automated recommendations, and make cost regressions visible via UI and evaluation harnesses. Summary of changes: - Autotune service: new microservice responsible for ingesting traffic histograms and producing recommended default configs (batching.window_ms, max_batch_size, prefix_cache_ttl). Includes simple RL-inspired policy that weighs latency SLO violations against per-token cost reduction. - Runtime integration: serving runtime now accepts a recommended_config payload and will apply it as the new "defaults" for route/model when in "autotune-managed" mode. Includes feature flags and granular opt-out. - Quantization profiles: added a registry format (json-based) and heuristics to select quant profiles per model family and target throughput/latency. Profiles are annotated with expected percentiles for latency impact and quality delta. - Unit-econ tooling: CLI command redwood uecon evaluate --profile <profile> that runs a simulated batch of requests against a local harness and reports cost-per-1k-tokens, tail latency, and estimated quality impact. Dashboard wiring added for per-customer reports and flagging when recommended configs would increase cost. - Telemetry and alerts: new metrics (autotune.recommendations.count, uecon.estimated_savings, quant.profile_selection.count) and dashboards. - Tests and docs: e2e tests for the autotune flow, unit tests for the quant-picker heuristics, and docs for operators. Migration notes: existing explicit route configs are not overwritten. Autotune recommendations are opt-in per-route by default. Operators can enable per-customer rollouts via the Console or CLI. Backwards compatibility: all runtime config endpoints keep previous behavior unless autotune-managed flag is enabled. Performance results: internal canary across 3 customers showed median token-cost reduction of ~18% with <2ms median latency regression and no measurable quality regressions on our eval sets. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked in Linear ENG-8423 - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] e2e canary run - [x] docs and Console wiring - [x] feature flag gated
commits: feat(autotune): add autotune microservice and API surface
feat(runtime): accept autotune recommended_config and apply as defaults
chore(quant): add quantization profile registry and selection heuristics
feat(uecon): add CLI 'redwood uecon evaluate' and dashboard metrics
test: add e2e canary test for autotune flow
docs: add operator docs and rollout guide
review_comments: Raj Patel: Nice work - can you add a short description of the reward function used by the autotuner in the design doc? Currently it's a little implicit.
Maya Chen (author): Added a paragraph to Linear ENG-8423 clarifying the reward function and its clipping for latency SLOs. Also added unit test for reward shaping.
Elena García: The quant profile selector looks good but we should ensure the selector prefers lower-quant models if quality drop exceeds threshold. Please add a configurable quality threshold.
Maya Chen (author): Added 'quant.quality_threshold' and default of 0.01 (1% allowed quality delta). Selector now emits a warning metric when threshold is hit.
Owen Park: e2e canary shows one customer with tail latency spikes at 99.9th percentile - looks tied to a rare long sequence workload. Suggest adding an override to pin max_batch_size per-route.
Maya Chen (author): Added per-route override and improved TTL-based cache invalidation for long sequences. Re-ran canary and 99.9p spikes are resolved.
discussion_summary: Reviewers requested clarification on reward function and a quality threshold for quant selection; both addressed by author. One canary customer revealed tail latency spike that required per-route overrides; resolved and re-canary passed.
merge_commit_message:
squash: cost-optimization: autotune defaults + quant profiles + uecon tooling

Autotune service, runtime integration, quant profiles, uecon CLI/dashboard, tests and docs.
release_notes: Added autotune-managed defaults for batching and caching, quantization profile registry with heuristic picker, and unit-economics tooling (CLI + dashboard). Autotune is opt-in and feature-flag gated. Expected median token-cost reduction ~18% in canary runs. Operators can opt out or pin per-route configs.
notes_for_ops: Autotune is behind feature flag 'autotune.enabled'. Default behavior is opt-in per-route. To enable globally for a customer: redwood console -> customer -> inference -> enable autotune or CLI 'redwood route set --autotune-managed true'. Monitor metrics: autotune.recommendations.count, uecon.estimated_savings. Rollback: disable flag or pin a route config to previous defaults.
